item.title: West Texas rancher rejected wind turbines twice; royalties now help keep his family ranch running
item.description: A fifth-generation West Texas rancher twice rejected wind turbines on his family property before agreeing to host seven turbines from the Cactus Flats wind project. Since 2019, the regular wind income has helped cover ranching costs, from livestock feed and workers to fences and repairs. The project also helped him invest in a community site in Menard, showing how wind royalties can support traditional ranching and rural development.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1966, Marlon Brando bought a private Polynesian atoll; it is now a wildlife sanctuary
item.description: Marlon Brando's private atoll now serves as a crucial marine conservation site. Thousands of green sea turtle hatchlings have been recorded after decades of protection efforts. Habitat restoration and invasive species removal significantly aided this environmental transformation. Eco-tourism at The Brando luxury resort helps fund ongoing scientific research and conservation initiatives. While nesting beaches are safe, turtles face dangers from fishing and plastic pollution at sea.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2021, Amazon shut US rooftop solar after six incidents at 47 sites; audit found 259 issues
item.description: Amazon shut down rooftop solar systems at all 47 of its North American sites in 2021 after six facilities reported fires or arc flash incidents. A later audit found one critical and 259 significant issues across its global solar portfolio, including mismatched connectors, improper installation, poor wire management and water intrusion in inverters.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1967, Guy Savy bought a Seychelles island; after restoring nesting habitat, its sooty tern colony...
item.description: Once threatened by severe ecological decline, Bird Island has transformed into a remarkable conservation achievement. Over decades of exploitation and farming, the island's environment was heavily damaged. However, when Guy Savy and partners took over in 1967, they began restoration and promoted eco-tourism. This initiative has led to a major recovery in seabird numbers, proving that long-term conservation can revitalize damaged ecosystems.

item.title: Astronomers hear a mysterious cosmic hum linked to strange dark stars from 13 billion years ago
item.description: Astronomers may have found a new way to investigate the Universe's first supermassive black holes. A faint gravitational-wave hum detected through pulsars could contain clues about ancient objects. Hypothetical Dark Stars, powered partly by dark matter, could have left black-hole descendants. These ancient black-hole seeds could grow and merge, producing part of the gravitational-wave background.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Iowa plant shreds Wind Turbine blades into fibres and powders for concrete, mortar and asphalt
item.description: Regen Fiber has opened a wind turbine blade recycling facility in Fairfax, Iowa, using an all-mechanical process that avoids heat and chemicals. The plant shreds old blades into fibres and additives for use in concrete, mortar and asphalt. It expects to process more than 30,000 tons of blades each year.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2019, a YouTuber was challenged to plant millions of trees, today his campaign has planted 25 million worldwide
item.description: MrBeast, the popular YouTuber, launched an ambitious initiative known as #TeamTrees. This groundbreaking campaign garnered viral attention, resulting in the planting of millions of trees funded by generous online donations. Partnering with various influencers and environmental organizations, it has successfully restored vast tracts of land and sequestered significant amounts of carbon. His innovative use of social media demonstrates how digital platforms can drive meaningful charitable endeavors.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 2013, Florida’s Tortuga Music Festival began restoring dunes with sea oats; 13 years later...
item.description: For over thirteen years, music enthusiasts and dedicated volunteers have joined forces to rejuvenate the dunes at Fort Lauderdale Beach, a tradition that began alongside the Tortuga Music Festival in 2013. By planting resilient sea oats, they bolster coastal defenses against storm surges and erosion, while also creating essential nesting grounds for sea turtles. This inspiring initiative exemplifies how large-scale public events can embrace sustainability.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Northern spotted owl once became a symbol of America’s logging wars; now scientists say it is already functionally extinct
item.description: The northern spotted owl, once a revered icon of environmental activism, faces dire circumstances as it becomes functionally extinct in numerous regions. A recent study indicates a severe decline in its populations throughout their historical habitat. Factors such as habitat destruction and rampant wildfires have severely impacted the species over the years, while the encroaching barred owl emerges as a formidable threat.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Chicago physicist’s 20-year-old quantum imaging theory gets experimental proof using superconductors
item.description: The University of Illinois Chicago’s Dirk Morr proposed a way to create high-resolution quantum images using superconductors two decades ago. A new experiment by researchers in Germany, supported by Morr’s theoretical model, has now produced quantum imaging similar to what he predicted, providing experimental confirmation of his earlier work.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In the 1940s, Nevada’s six-week divorce law turned a 1,627-acre ranch into a refuge for women seeking quick divorces; now it is becoming the state’s 28th park
item.description: Transforming from a historic divorce haven into a state park, Nevada's Lower Carson Ranch now spans 1,627 acres alongside the Carson River, preserving crucial wildlife habitats. This transition marks the end of 155 years of private ownership, officially now under Nevada State Parks. While development for future public use is underway and access is limited, the community is actively participating in selecting a new name for the park.

item.title: Russia prepares for ‘massive strikes’ against Ukraine's energy facilities
item.description: Amid rising tensions, Russia announced plans for large-scale attacks aimed at Ukraine's energy infrastructure, following strikes on its own civilian areas. A recent attack in Bucha tragically resulted in thirty-seven fatalities. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy called out perceived negligence in ammunition storage practices. As these aerial campaigns escalate, the region faces a deepening crisis with infrastructure under relentless assault.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Texas WWII veteran’s remarkable century is being celebrated with a heartfelt tribute
item.description: Weldon Kenneth Bowen, a centenarian and World War II veteran from Texas, is commemorating his 100th birthday in style. The Texas Veterans Land Board has launched a campaign urging individuals to send 100 birthday cards to this distinguished Marine Corps veteran, who selflessly served during the war’s final months and earned the Good Conduct Medal. This effort not only recognizes his service but also celebrates his extraordinary life.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: NASA tests GPS-free navigation using other satellites and space debris as landmarks
item.description: NASA has tested FALCON, a system that lets satellites navigate without GPS by using other spacecraft and orbital debris as reference points. During a three-day test, the system autonomously improved the known orbits of more than 200 space objects while also calculating the position of NASA’s Starling spacecraft.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 750 dead, 20,000 deployed as rising rivers hamper rescue ops
item.description: Nepal and Tibet floods have claimed 750 lives and left over 3,000 missing. Rescuers continue operations amid warnings of fresh flooding and difficult conditions. Hundreds are believed trapped in hydropower tunnels, requiring specialized international assistance. India and China are providing crucial support including forensic experts and relief supplies. Infrastructure damage has cut off communities, while aid efforts are ongoing.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: American startup raises $180 million to drill rock over 5km deep to build world's first superhot geothermal plant at 500 °C
item.description: Quaise Energy has successfully raised $180 million for its groundbreaking superhot geothermal plant initiative. Utilizing cutting-edge microwave technology, the project vaporizes rock instead of using conventional drill bits. Collaboration with Nabors Industries will provide essential drilling expertise and equipment. The Obsidian Project, located in Oregon, is set to generate 50 MW by 2030, paving the way for a sustainable energy future.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A Colombian man struggling to build his own home created Lego-like bricks from recycled plastic
item.description: A Colombian architect helped develop Lego-like building blocks made from recycled plastic and rubber to create temporary and permanent homes. The system was used to build shelters for 42 displaced families in Guapi in 2015. Four people could assemble a 40-square-metre house in five days, without using glue, cement or water.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
